newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-CHANG EXTENDED TO THREE SETS BY MICHAEL JOYCE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG EXTENDED TO THREE SETS BY MICHAEL JOYCE.

text.p: Top seed and defending champion Michael Chang again was extended to three sets at the $675,000 Legg Mason Tennis Classic, this time by Michael Joyce, 163rd in the world rankings, in the third round.
Chang, ranked second in the world, ultimately prevailed 4-6 6-1 6-2, after having had to come back from two service breaks in the third set Tuesday night and get past Mexican qualifier Luis Herrera.
All along, Chang has been saying there is "great depth in tennis these days and no one can be taken lightly."

Chang, who now has won 25 of 28 matches on hardcourts in 1997, said there was no particular aspect of his game bothering him right now. "Everything can be better and solidified. My complete game is not there yet, but I am competing well," he said.
The key to his victory over Joyce was his serve. He cracked 15 aces and said: "It helped me out quite a bit, getting some free points, particularly against a player who returns well like Joyce does."

David Wheaton, a serve and volleyer who climbed to a world ranking of 17 in 1991 but who has not been in the top 100 since suffering an Achilles' tendon injury early last year, continued his comeback with a 3-6 7-6 7-6 victory over fifth-seeded Jason Stoltenberg of Australia.
